clue.text: Inability to make out after a fall?

definitions.text: Inability to make out after a fall?

parts.words: Inability to make out after a fall?
parts.note: the fall is not a tumble but a fall of snow, whose glare can leave a person unable to see

explanation.surface: Someone who has taken a tumble finds they cannot think straight.
explanation.definitionFit: Glare off fresh snow can temporarily damage the eyes, a condition that stops the sufferer making things out.

clue.text: One who, in turn, may take in Toledo?

definitions.text: One who, in turn, may take in Toledo?

parts.words: One who, in turn, may take in Toledo?
parts.note: Toledo steel was famed for blades, so a Toledo is a blade; a turn is a music-hall act, where a performer takes one down the throat

explanation.surface: Someone who, in rotation, visits a Spanish city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take in' looks like sightseeing, and 'turn' like taking turns; a turn is a stage act.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideshow performer swallows blades, and a Toledo is a fine Spanish blade.

clue.text: Plump, round bees swarming

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: bees swarming move in a confused mass, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Fat rotund insects buzzing about.
explanation.definitionFit: Being very fat or overweight goes well beyond plumpness, but the two are close synonyms.

clue.text: Great Tom, say, double or treble player?

parts.note: Great Tom is the famous bell at Christ Church, Oxford
a ringer is a lookalike or double

explanation.surface: A big man known as Tom, a singer of two parts.
explanation.walkthrough: The treble is the highest bell in a ring, so its player is a campanologist; 'double' and 'treble' seem to be voice parts.
explanation.definitionFit: In church bell-ringing the lightest bell is the treble, rung by one of the band.

clue.text: Batting, established oneself and was never out

parts.note: a cricketer batting is said to be in
to have settled or lived somewhere is to have dwelt there

explanation.surface: A cricketer at the crease settles in and is never dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the side batting is 'in'; 'never out' continues the cricket picture but means staying within.
explanation.definitionFit: To have abided inside something is to have remained within it and never left.

clue.text: Empty day, unpleasant as a rule

indicators.note: an empty word has its inside letters removed, leaving just its first and last letters

parts.note: nasty means unpleasant

explanation.surface: A blank, disagreeable day, as is normally the case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as a rule' looks like 'usually'; 'rule' is the definition, 'as a' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A succession of rulers from one family holds power, so the word stands for a reign.

clue.text: Work-unit on oxygen for that reason

parts.note: the erg is a unit of work in the CGS system
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A measure of energy placed on a gas, so it follows.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin word means therefore, introducing a conclusion.

clue.text: Stifles to trouble horses

definitions.meaning: a contagious bacterial infection of the throat in horses

explanation.definitionFit: To choke is the verb sense, and the noun is an equine throat disease.

clue.text: It will blow up in re entry, logic orders

indicators.note: orders here means the letters are put in a new sequence

explanation.surface: Logic demands a safe re-entry, or there will be an explosion.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 're-entry'; 'orders' is the anagram signal, rearranging IN RE ENTRY LOGIC.
explanation.definitionFit: The oily liquid is a powerful explosive, the active ingredient in dynamite.

clue.text: Having done, left port with too much cargo

parts.note: something done or finished is over
Aden is a port in Yemen

explanation.surface: A ship, its business finished, sails from harbour dangerously loaded.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel loaded beyond its capacity is weighed down with more freight than it should carry.

clue.text: Maxim sounds clumsy

indicators.note: the word for clumsy is to be heard rather than read, giving a writer's surname

parts.note: gawky means awkward or clumsy

explanation.surface: A saying comes across as awkward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maxim' looks like a saying; it is the first name of the Russian writer Maxim Gorky (also spelt Gorki). The sound match works in a British accent that drops the R.
explanation.definitionFit: Maxim Gorki was the Russian author of The Lower Depths, so the forename stands for his surname.

clue.text: Fourth-class train is comfortless

parts.note: D is the fourth grade after A, B and C
to train or bring up children is to rear them

explanation.surface: A slow fourth-class railway service offers no comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' looks like a railway service, but it is the verb meaning bring up.
explanation.definitionFit: Drear is a poetic form of dreary, describing something bleak and cheerless.

clue.text: Comfortable middy?

definitions.meaning: Mr Midshipman ... is the hero of Frederick Marryat's 1836 naval novel; a middy is a midshipman

explanation.definitionFit: Being relaxed is a synonym, and Marryat's fictional junior naval officer bears that surname.

clue.text: Remarkable person a setback for gambling centre

indicators.note: a setback here means the gambling town's name is set back, read from its end

parts.note: Reno in Nevada is famous for its casinos

explanation.surface: An outstanding individual suffers a reverse at a casino town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setback' looks like a misfortune but signals RENO turned round, ONER.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-off, a person unlike any other, is British slang for someone exceptional.

clue.text: Board having a pick-me-up on sea-food

parts.note: a plank is a board of timber
a tonic is a restorative pick-me-up

explanation.surface: A diner at a table enjoys a reviving drink with fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is an adjective, so 'on sea-food' (about drifting marine organisms that feed sea creatures) is the definition; 'having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective concerns the tiny drifting organisms that form the base of the ocean food chain.

clue.text: A trivial thing that can be shelved!

definitions.meaning: a piece of furniture with open shelves for ornaments

explanation.definitionFit: The word is used for any odd trifle, and also for a Victorian stand of tiers for displaying knick-knacks.

clue.text: Dangerous gas of mine following dripping?

parts.note: after means following
something dripping is damp

explanation.surface: A hazardous fume in a pit after leaks.
explanation.definitionFit: The toxic gas left in a colliery after an explosion of firedamp, rich in carbon monoxide.

clue.text: Brand of Christmas cheer you will book, say?

indicators.note: say means the phrase is to be spoken, giving a festive item

parts.note: you'll is the short form of you will, and to book is to log, so this says you'll log

explanation.surface: An invitation to reserve some festive fun.
explanation.walkthrough: A brand here is a burning piece of wood, not a trade name.
explanation.definitionFit: A large log burnt in the hearth at Christmas is a traditional piece of seasonal warmth and good cheer.

clue.text: Learning lines

definitions.meaning: scholarship, as in a man of ...
short written messages: drop me a line

explanation.definitionFit: Literary scholarship is called this, and written correspondence consists of them.

clue.text: Aramis, the second of Dumas's disguised warriors out east

indicators.note: disguised means the letters are hidden in a new arrangement
the second of picks the second letter of the word

explanation.surface: One of the Three Musketeers, in disguise, among Dumas's fighters.
explanation.walkthrough: Aramis is one of Dumas's Three Musketeers, a natural first thought for 'warriors'; the definition is Japanese warriors.
explanation.definitionFit: The hereditary military caste of feudal Japan fought for their lords in the Far East.

clue.text: Many set free in condonation

indicators.note: free means the letters are released from their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A large number are released under an official pardon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' looks part of the story of release but is the anagram signal on MANY SET.
explanation.definitionFit: A general pardon is an official overlooking or forgiving of offences.

clue.text: Footballers magazine

definitions.meaning: a store for weapons and ammunition

explanation.definitionFit: The north London club takes its name from Woolwich, whose weapons store is the other sense.

clue.text: Unmatched piece of the sporran

indicators.note: piece of means a run of letters is taken from inside the word sporran

explanation.surface: A single odd item from a Highland purse.
explanation.walkthrough: A sporran is the pouch worn on the front of a Scottish kilt. Orra is a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots the word means odd or occasional, as of something left without its pair.

clue.text: Prophet here knocked back an intoxicating drink

indicators.note: drinks are knocked back, but here the drink's name is turned to read backwards

parts.note: soma is the intoxicating ritual drink of Vedic India

explanation.surface: A holy man in this place downed a strong drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like drinking; it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Amos is a minor prophet of the Old Testament with a book named after him.

clue.text: Eat small amounts — it makes sense

definitions.meaning: to sample food a little at a time
one of the five senses, perceived by the tongue

explanation.definitionFit: Sampling food a little is the verb sense, and the noun is the sense of flavour.

clue.text: Reject drive north?

parts.note: to spur is to drive or urge on

explanation.surface: Refusing a journey northwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To scorn or turn away is a synonym for rebuff.

clue.text: Slight advantage of golf chub without tungsten head

indicators.note: without means the letter is left out of the word

parts.note: a wedge is a golf club for lofted shots
W is the chemical symbol for tungsten

explanation.surface: A golfer's small edge from a club lacking a metal head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' says the tungsten letter comes off the front of WEDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a narrow lead over a rival is a common idiom for a small superiority.

clue.text: Antelope of eastern district?

parts.note: a land is a region or district

explanation.surface: Asking which antelope comes from the east.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large African antelope with spiralled horns.

clue.text: Spearworts, for example, uncurl in a flurry

indicators.note: in a flurry the letters are thrown about and rearranged

explanation.surface: Wild plants unfurling quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal is 'flurry'; IN and A belong to the fodder with UNCURL.
explanation.definitionFit: Spearworts are buttercups, members of the plant genus Ranunculus, so they are examples of the genus.

clue.text: Freedom of speech in Dunbar, say?

definitions.text: Freedom of speech in Dunbar, say?

parts.words: Freedom of speech in Dunbar, say?
parts.note: Dunbar is the Scottish makar William Dunbar, and the freedom is a writer's licence to bend rules of language

explanation.surface: Asking about free expression in a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Dunbar is a town in East Lothian, but here it is William Dunbar, the medieval Scottish poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Writers of verse are allowed to depart from normal grammar or fact for effect, a liberty in how they express things.
